facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Gualicho was discovered on February 13, 2007, by Akiko Shinya near the Ezequiel Ramos Mexía Reservoir.
facts.quote: On 13 February 2007, Akiko Shinya, preparator of the Field Museum of Natural History, east of the Ezequiel Ramos Mexía Reservoir at the Rancho Violante, discovered the skeleton of a theropod new to science.

facts.statement: Gualicho was formally named and described in 2016 by Sebastián Apesteguía, Nathan D. Smith, Rubén Juárez Valieri, and Peter J. Makovicky.
facts.quote: In 2016, the specimen was named and described by Sebastián Apesteguía, Nathan D. Smith, Rubén Juárez Valieri and Peter J. Makovicky.

facts.statement: The genus name Gualicho is derived from the gualichu, a demon from local folklore.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the gualichu, a demon of local folklore.

facts.statement: The specific name shinyae honors Akiko Shinya, the discoverer of the specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Shinya as the animal's discoverer.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, MPCN PV 0001, is a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
facts.quote: The holotype, MPCN PV 0001, consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: Many bones of the holotype were found in their original anatomical positions, though much of the skeleton was destroyed by erosion.
facts.quote: Most bones were uncovered in their original anatomical position but much of the skeleton had been destroyed by erosion.

facts.statement: Gualicho lived during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 106 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossils were found in the Huincul Formation, dating to the Albian stage of the lower Cretaceous Period, around 106 million years ago.

facts.statement: Gualicho shinyae lived during the Cenomanian stage of the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 93 million years ago, in what is now Argentina.
facts.quote: Gualicho shinyae es la única especie conocida del género extinto Gualicho de dinosaurio terópodo averrostre que vivió a mediados del periodo Cretácico, hace unos 93 millones de años durante el Cenomaniense en lo que es hoy Sudamérica en Argentina.

facts.statement: Gualicho was 6 to 7 meters long and possessed reduced arms with possibly two functional fingers, though a 2020 study suggests a third finger may have been present.
facts.quote: the 6-7 m Gualicho possesses reduced arms and possibly two fingered hands, although a 2020 study suggests enough of the third metacarpal is present for a third finger.

facts.statement: Gualicho is described as a medium-sized theropod with strong, agile legs and reduced arms with only two functional fingers.
facts.quote: Se describe como un terópodo de tamaño mediano que poseía piernas fuertes y ágiles así como brazos reducidos con manos provistas de solo dos dedos funcionales.

facts.statement: Gualicho measured between 6 and 7 meters in length and 1.70 meters in height.
facts.quote: Medía de 6 a 7 metros de largo y 1,70 metros de altura.

facts.statement: Gualicho inhabited what is now northern Argentine Patagonia, which was then part of the South American island continent separated from Gondwana.
facts.quote: Habitó en lo que ahora es el norte de la Patagonia argentina, en lo que fue entonces la isla-continente de Suramérica que se había separado del resto del supercontinente de Gondwana.

facts.statement: Fossils of Gualicho were found in the Huincul Formation, dating from the late Cenomanian to early Turonian stages of the Cretaceous, about 93 million years ago.
facts.quote: Los fósiles fueron hallados en la Formación Huincul, la cual data de finales de la época del Cenomaniense a inicios del Turoniense del período Cretácico, hace unos 93 millones de años.

facts.statement: The environment where Gualicho lived 93 million years ago in Río Negro Province featured a warm climate with large rivers, where it coexisted with giants like Mapusaurus and Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: La zona de la Provincia de Río Negro en la que vivió hace 93 millones de años gozaba de un clima cálido y grandes ríos, lugares en los que convivió con otros dinosaurios conocidos incluyendo algunos gigantes tales como Mapusaurus y Argentinosaurus.

facts.statement: It has been informally suggested on blogs that Gualicho is synonymous with the megaraptoran Aoniraptor due to similarities in their caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Gualicho has been informally suggested on blogs to be synonymous with the megaraptoran Aoniraptor, also known from Huincul Formation and uncovered at the Violante site in view of similarities in their caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: A 2020 comparative analysis of pneumatic structures found many differences between Gualicho and Aoniraptor, challenging their synonymy.
facts.quote: Aranciaga Rolando et al. in 2020 performed a comparative analysis between the pneumatic structures of Aoniraptor and Gualicho, and found many differences between the two.

facts.statement: In 2025, Calvo and colleagues concluded that Gualicho is not closely related to megaraptorans like Megaraptor due to significant morphological differences in the humerus.
facts.quote: In 2025, Calvo and colleagues compared the humerus of Gualicho to that of other megaraptorans including a specimen of adult Megaraptor, and concluded that this taxon is not closely related to them due to significant morphological differences.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that Gualicho's humerus shares similarities with various coelurosaur groups, making a confident referral to a specific theropod clade difficult.
facts.quote: They also noted that the features of its humerus shares many similarities to various groups of coelurosaurs, so a confident referral within a specific clade of theropods cannot be made.

facts.statement: In 2025, Delcourt et al. recovered Gualicho and Deltadromeus as sister taxa within Ornithomimosauria based on phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: In their comprehensive revision of Santanaraptor and Mirischia, Delcourt et al. (2025) recovered Deltadromeus and Gualicho as sister taxa within Ornithomimosauria based on both equal and implied weight phylogenetic analyses.

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis by Apesteguía et al. placed Gualicho within the clade Carcharodontosauria.
facts.quote: The cladogram below follows a 2016 analysis by Apesteguía et al., with Gualicho within Carcharodontosauria:

facts.statement: Gualicho is classified within the unranked family Neotheropoda.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Neotheropoda

facts.statement: Gualicho belongs to the unranked genus Averostra.
facts.quote: unranked_genus: Averostra

facts.statement: The genus Gualicho was established by Apesteguía et al. in 2016.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Apesteguía et al., 2016

facts.statement: The species Gualicho shinyae was described by Apesteguía et al. in 2016.
facts.quote: species_authority: Apesteguía et al., 2016

facts.statement: Nototyrannus violantei is listed as a synonym of Gualicho shinyae, though it is considered a nomen nudum.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Nototyrannus violantei Anónimo, 2011 (nomen nudum)

facts.statement: If Gualicho is considered a carnosaur, its two functional fingers might indicate convergent evolution of limb reduction similar to tyrannosaurids and abelisaurids.
facts.quote: La presencia de dos dedos funcionales en sus extremidades superiores podría indicar que los carnosaurios estuvieron sujetos de forma convergente a la misma tendencia hacia la reducción de los brazos que ocurrió en la evolución de los tiranosáuridos y los abelisáuridos, siempre que Gualicho sea considerado un carnosaurio en primer lugar.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether Gualicho's relatives, the megaraptorans and neovenatorids, were carnosaurs or theropods more closely related to ceratosaurs than to carnosaurs.
facts.quote: Filogenéticamente, Gualicho presenta dos posibilidades; que los megarraptoranos y los neovenatóridos fueran carnosaurios, o que los megarraptoranos y neovenatóridos fueran una gradación de terópodos más cercanamente relacionados con los celurosaurios que a los carnosaurios.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that Gualicho might be a synonym of the megaraptoran Aoniraptor, which was found at the Violante site in the Huincul Formation, based on similarities in their tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Se ha sugerido que Gualicho podría ser un sinónimo del megarraptorano Aoniraptor, el cual también es conocido de la Formación Huincul y descubierto en el sitio Violante, en vista de las similitudes existentes en sus vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: Aoniraptor is likely an invalid name (nomen nudum) because it does not meet the requirements of ICZN article 8.5.3.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Aoniraptor no cumple con los requisitos del artículo 8.5.3 del ICZN, lo que significa que es probablemente un nomen nudum sin validez.

facts.statement: A 2025 analysis comparing Gualicho's humerus to adult Megaraptor concluded that Gualicho is not closely related to megaraptorans due to significant morphological differences.
facts.quote: En 2025, Calvo y colaboradores publicaron un análisis en que compararon el húmero de Gualicho al de los megarraptores incluyendo a un espécimen adulto de Megaraptor, y concluyeron que este taxón no se encuentra cercanamente a ellos debido a que tiene diferencias morfológicas significativas.

facts.statement: Because Gualicho's humerus shares similarities with various groups of ceratosaurs, researchers cannot assign the animal to a specific theropod clade with certainty.
facts.quote: Ellos también señalaron que su húmero comparte similitudes con el de varios grupos de celurosaurios, por lo cual no puede hacerse una asignación certera del animal a un clado específico de terópodos.

facts.statement: Gualicho lived during the Albian stage, between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Gualicho is Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: Gualicho is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

rejected.statement: Gualicho lived in what is now northern Patagonia, on a South American island continent separated from Gondwana.
rejected.quote: It lived in what is now northern Patagonia, on what was then a South American island continent split off from the supercontinent Gondwana.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'lived in what is now northern Patagonia on'

rejected.statement: A 2018 analysis by Porfiri et al. placed Gualicho within Coelurosauria, differing from earlier analyses by including additional megaraptoran taxa.
rejected.quote: Although the results are different, with Gualicho within Coelurosauria, the methodology analysis was practically identical to that of Apesteguia et al. (2016), only differing in the fact that it incorporated Tratayenia and Murusraptor, two megaraptorans not sampled in the analysis of Apesteguia et al.
